translation.title: Amorolfine Nail Lacquer
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for onychomycosis (fungal infection of the fingernails and toenails) caused by dermatophytes, yeasts and molds, when the infection covers 80% or less of the nail surface.
translation.usage: Apply it to the infected fingernails or toenails once or twice a week. Before applying, file down the infected part of the nail - especially the nail surface - as completely as possible with the enclosed nail file, then wipe the nail surface with an enclosed pad to remove any oil, and be sure to wipe off any remaining lacquer with a pad. Then, using the enclosed reusable spatula, apply the lacquer over the entire surface of the infected nail and let it dry. Each time you treat an infected nail, dip the spatula into the bottle; do not wipe the excess off on the rim of the bottle, and after applying, clean the spatula thoroughly with one of the pads used for wiping the nails. Continue the treatment without interruption until the nail has grown back and the infected area is completely healed. The treatment period depends on the severity and location of the infection - usually about 6 months for fingernails and 9 to 12 months for toenails.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it or have had a hypersensitivity reaction to it, in infants and children, if you have inflammatory changes of the skin around the nail, or if you have a blood circulation disorder, malnutrition or alcohol dependence. Women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women, must not use this medicine. Do not use a nail file that has been used on an infected nail on a healthy person's nails. This medicine is for external use only - take care that it does not touch the eyes, nose, mouth or other mucous membranes. If you use nail polish, apply it at least 10 minutes after applying this medicine, and remove the nail polish completely before applying the medicine again. When working with organic solvents (such as paint thinner or gasoline), wear solvent-proof gloves to protect the lacquer on your nails. Avoid using artificial nails while using this medicine. Adverse reactions may occur - uncommonly a whole-body allergic reaction, and rarely nail disorders, nail discoloration, nail breakage, splitting of the nail, contact dermatitis, redness, itching, rash or blisters; if they do, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature, keep out of reach of children, and close the cap tightly right after use so that the solution does not dry out.
